newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Former U.S. president Carter sees Nigeria's Abacha.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. president Carter sees Nigeria's Abacha.

text.p: Former United States president Jimmy Carter met Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha on Sunday to discuss next month's Liberian elections, U.S. embassy officials said.
The officials said Carter was meeting Abacha in his capacity as head of the Economic Community of West African States, which sponsors the Nigerian-led ECOMOG peacekeeping force in Liberia.
"He is here to see how his organisation (The Carter Centre) can help with elections in Liberia," one U.S. official said.
Liberia, founded by freed American slaves, is due to hold elections on July 19, under a West African peace plan to end over seven years of civil war which have killed an estimated 150,000 people.

Nigerian newspapers speculated that Carter would also discuss Nigeria's detention of political prisoners and its own plans to restore democracy in 1998, but U.S. officials said the visit had nothing to do with Nigeria's internal politics.
Military-ruled Nigeria's relations with Western nations are strained for lack of democracy and alleged human rights abuses.
On Monday Carter will discuss the eradication of Guinea worm, a parasite spread through dirty water in parts of tropical Africa, with Nigeria's health minister.
